In this part, we focused on the army and warfare. How will the anarchist territory hold up in the fight against the state? And how will wars be fought in the future? Why is it so easy to wage war nowadays?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Polycentric versus centralized law
desc:
Classical liberal Andrej Poleščuk invited me to his stream, where we discussed centralized and decentralized law. At first we dealt with classic evolutionary arguments, but towards the end we got to some interesting analyses; in the record you will also find a theoretical justification for why polycentric legal systems converge to the NAP (however, it is a very advanced chapter, we go deeper than in the Polis judiciary lecture).

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Cryptocurrencies
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on cryptocurrencies. We were not so much technical, but more concerned with the economic side of things; and cryptocurrencies as the money of the future.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: The Labor Market
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on the labor market without regulations. Who do they actually help? And who does employee protection protect? On the contrary, who does it harm?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: General Basics for Everyone
desc:
I was contacted by the owner of the Centrála club - which some jokingly and aptly call Decentralá with respect to the other program - and asked for a lecture: Ankap for beginners. If you have no idea what this is all about, this lecture explains the absolute basics of this school of thought. I tried to lecture in such a way that absolutely everyone could understand; I hope I managed to do it at least in general.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/decentrala/

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Conference Education for the Future
desc:
Mensa CR, the World of Education, the National Institute for Further Education and the Fraus Publishing House jointly organized the Education for the Future conference, which took place on Friday, March 2, 2018 and Saturday, March 3, 2018 in Prague. I gladly accepted their invitation to lecture as well; I chose the complete separation of education from the state as a topic, which probably won't surprise anyone.


– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Healthcare
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on free market healthcare, pharmaceutical production, regulations in medicine and healthcare certifications.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Urza in Stigur's Darth Night Show
desc:
Pavel Stigur Novák watched my stream with Zvědátory; then he made an unflattering comment on him on his show. I offered him if he would do the same, if I could oppose him; he agreed. The stream ended up being quite beneficial, we focused on a few topics in depth, which is actually great. We discussed teachers and education, then the death cycle of democracy and how state protection of the irresponsible creates more irresponsible. I think the footage is definitely worth watching.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Nineteen: In the Broader Context...
desc:
How to go from a huge omnivorous state to anarcho-capitalism? And where does the road definitely not lead? We will also talk about this at the last regular lecture of this cycle. Many of you have rightly noted that most of the lectures were "one-of-a-kind" in the sense of applying the same principle to various branches of human endeavor. I would like to clarify and formulate this principle in general terms; especially for those who didn't notice it. And finally, we will place anarcho-capitalism in some context of the other anarchist schools, of which there are many and about which you will certainly hear a lot more.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Scouts: Anarcho-Capitalism
desc:
My favorite YouTuber (and probably the only one I follow) Martin Rota invited me to the program Zvědátoři, which he has been doing for a long time with Patrik Kořenář; the topic was - how else but - anarcho-capitalism!
And I have to say, it was a great discussion for me; Martin Rota is a logician, he has great arguments and overall he is one of the best opponents. Plus, I think live is even better than online. So I hope you enjoy watching the video at least half as much as I enjoyed making it.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Lecture for the Gymnasium on the Victory Plain
desc:
I accepted an invitation to a lecture at Gymnasium Na Vítězné pláni to tell the students there something about anarcho-capitalism. A surprisingly large number of students came to the lecture; although they had many lectures to choose from, there weren't enough chairs in the end, so they had to sit on the furniture. They asked great questions; I consider the whole debate to be very constructive. Above all, in the end it turned out that almost everyone learned something new!

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Social Issues
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this piece, we addressed the devastating effects of the welfare state on our society; and how would we be without him?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Eighteen: The Army
desc:
As difficult as the free market provision of justice and internal security is, defense against an external enemy and, by extension, international relations represent by far the greatest challenge for a stateless anarcho-capitalist society. Can free people without a state defend themselves against aggressive conquerors? And if not, what will happen in the conquered territory? How does the control of a conquered anarchist territory differ from the control of a conquered state? Can the common survive without the state? Minarchists do not believe this; anarcho-capitalists do. Don't miss a lecture with a discussion on this interesting topic.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Education
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on education and its complete separation from the state, but also its function as a powerful propaganda tool.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Seventeen: Law Enforcement
desc:
If the lecture on the judiciary was controversial, it is doubly so for law enforcement. While last time we only dealt with disputes in which both parties more or less cooperate, this time we will talk about cases of criminals and desperadoes who violate property rights and actively try to avoid the administration of justice. How will the free market deal with them? Isn't the state really needed here? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Launch of the book Anarchocapitalism
desc:
Something I believe in has become more real and tangible because of me; I was able to celebrate this alongside my beloved wife, surrounded by people who believe in the same ideals, peacefully participate in their promotion, and without whom what is happening right now could never have happened, because without their hard work and support, all my efforts would have meant nothing. Thanks; thanks to all of you.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD); creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Senseless imprisonment
desc:
An 18-year-old girl got behind the wheel, recorded and streamed her actions until she killed her own sister live. There is no need to comment on how devastating this idea was, after all, she herself described it very aptly: "I killed my own sister just because I wanted to look cool." What about her now? Six years in prison! That's not much for a wasted life. But what good does it do?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Economic Calculation
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on economic calculation, its impossibility in central planning and some principles of the Austrian school of economics.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: CZPodcast
desc:
Roman Pichlík and Jiří Fabián invited me to their podcast; although the latter is almost always about programming, this time they wanted to talk about anarcho-capitalism, which of course pleased me and I gladly accepted. I really enjoyed getting to know them; it was interesting. In the discussion I was opposed by Karel Holub, whom I appreciate for his calm insight. I wish everyone a pleasant listening experience!

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Money and Banking
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this installment we covered money and banking; we also touched lightly on economic calculation and the function of money.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Jail, lose for all
desc:
On my way to work, I heard a message on the radio that I wanted to respond to immediately, so this recording was created; it was taken directly in the car, so I apologize for the slightly worse quality, but I think you can understand them. Two people committed something that was unfortunately not a victimless crime and were also guilty in terms of the NAP; on the other hand, I don't even agree with their imprisonment. Why? You will find out when you play the video.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: An Introduction
desc:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this work, we focused on the roots of anarcho-capitalism, its foundations and general principles; we also lightly honed in on specific topics, which we will certainly get to in more detail over time.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Cryptocurrencies and Anarcho-Capitalism
desc:
I accepted the invitation of the Prague Business Club for a lecture and discussion about cryptocurrencies and anarcho-capitalism. Interesting debates accompanied the whole evening; I would like to share a recording of one of its parts with you here. Unfortunately, the picture and sound starts from a third of the recording, for which I apologize; the reasons are bizarre (related to the line: "Teresa, please turn off that microphone." xD). I wish you a pleasant listening.
– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: NAP and cryptocurrency ownership
desc:
It was an honor to speak at the Bitcoin is Retro! Slovak Parallel Polis, Progressbar and Students for Liberty organized a great event and asked me to give a lecture on a purely theoretical topic, which really suited me - an old theoretician. Then followed a great discussion with an ending that you can look forward to (probably for a few months).
– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Sixteen: The Judiciary
desc:
How could a free market without states ensure a functioning judiciary? Who would appoint a judge? And would it be possible to appeal against the judgment? Is there any way to prevent the courts from favoring rich and wealthy clients? I will try to answer these - and many other - questions during the lecture; but first of all we get to the most interesting part: What would the courts decide if there was no central authority with a monopoly on legislation? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Anarcho-capitalism: a public cause
desc:
Anarcho-capitalism is finally being talked about! We are overwhelmed with questions and comments, the topic has already reached Jakub Janda from European values. A lot of people who don't know anything about anarcho-capitalism are also commenting now, but that's only good; please stay with us, be patient and help us spread the ideas of freedom!

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Anarcho-Capitalism Volume Fifteen: The Environment
desc:
Do we need states in order not to devastate nature and the environment? If our society is only "managed" by the free market, will we leave our descendants with more than just contaminated water, air and soil? Without the state, who would protect endangered animal species? And how to promote sustainable development without the state? To explain this interesting issue, I will make considerable use of the knowledge of the Austrian school of economics, which we discussed (mostly repeatedly) in previous lectures; I highly recommend refreshing them again.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Anarcho-capitalist revolution?
desc:
Left-wing anarchists are often revolutionaries; anarcho-capitalists typically do not. However, we are individualists, as a matter of principle we do not group together and we are united, among other things, by our reluctance to blindly obey authorities, so there are exceptions to each of our "typicals". On the one hand, this is great, but on the other hand, in this particular case, I consider it extremely important to say a few words about it...

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Urza in StandaShow
desc:
Youtuber Standa invited me to his online streaming show; and it was definitely an interesting interview. We talked about anarcho-capitalism; in the end, the audience could also ask their questions. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to go too deep, but thousands of people saw it, which I'm really happy about.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Fourteen: Healthcare
desc:
When the word "free market health care" is mentioned, most people immediately think of exorbitant amounts of money for medical procedures that the common mortal simply cannot afford to pay, leaving him with no choice but to live in sickness; or even die. Without the government, how could we afford to pay for medical care? Who would supervise the quality? How to overcome the enormous information asymmetry between doctor and patient in the market? Isn't free market healthcare an antisocial and horrible system through which the powerful can squeeze the powerless and sick? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions when you come to the lecture; and you can ask your own questions in the subsequent discussion.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Crowdfunding
desc:
https://kniha.urza.cz/

Thank you for your amazing support that makes the project so successful; we posted more rewards and we still haven't heard back from all the donors.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Where does statism come from?
desc:
Where do states get their power? Power is where one believes it to be; it's a trick, a shadow on the wall. And not only the shadow, but also the coat of arms, the image of the president and other religious symbols; we are all exposed to indoctrination by state propaganda from an early age...
Screenplay: Urza
Reads: Urza
Graphics: Tereza Vyslužilová

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Thirteen: The Labor Market
desc:
Do you think that without the state and its regulations, employees would have no standing, so employers could screw them over? In that case, this lecture is just for you! We will show why a free and unregulated labor market would not only not harm employees, but would, on the contrary, improve their situation in many ways; because the state provides its "protection" to employees as a bit of a disservice. Seeing exactly how and why this is so is not at all difficult; just come to the lecture, where we will talk about child labor and many other interesting things, among other things.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Panel Discussion "Anarcho-Capitalists and Elections"
desc:
In Parallel Polis, five anarcho-capitalists (four panelists and a moderator) gathered for a panel discussion about elections. I find the debate very interesting and beneficial; it contained arguments for and against participation in the elections, all from the position of staunch opponents of the state. Unfortunately, due to a technical fault, the last third of the recording is missing.

Discussing: Alice Eliška Hrazdilová, Pavol Lupták, Jan Hubík and Urza.
Moderator: Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD)

title: Media campaign
desc:
https://kniha.urza.cz/

Through the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism, we are working to get this topic into the media and thus spark a public discussion about a stateless society. Please help us get libertarian ideas to the people! Thank you

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Drugs and Liberty (SfL): Peace on Drugs
desc:
Presentation Peace on Drugs at Drugs and Liberty conference organized by Students for Liberty.
The global war on drugs has failed, with devastating consequences for individuals and societies around the world. Make peace on drugs then!

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Twelve: The Social System
desc:
Without the state, not only would there be no social benefits and unemployment support, but above all there would be no pension system as we know it now. What would that mean? In a free market society, would the poor starve to death on the streets? What would old people do without the state? I am going to answer these and many other questions at the twelfth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle; subsequently we can talk about these topics in a discussion.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Lecture for the OKO Society
desc:
The OKO association asked Freedom of Learning (with a capital S) for a lecture on the topic of Freedom of Learning (with a small s). The parents of the schoolchildren, but even the representatives of the city, arrived at the lecture; the reactions were surprisingly positive.
Although it was already possible to arrange the sound in such a way that I could be understood well, unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the questions from the audience, for which I apologize. The presentation on the wall was glossy, so it couldn't be caught on camera; making videos is not as easy as it might seem.

– Urza for Freedom of Learning

title: The book "Anarcho-Capitalism"
desc:
Support the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism:
http://kniha.urza.cz/

title: HCPP17: Liberate education from the state!
desc:
Compulsory school attendance is not only immoral, but it also represents the initial reason for our economic lack of freedom; State education costs money, also it's a source of state propaganda and statist indoctrination. This is the main cause of the conviction of people that the free market fails in so many areas, so we need the state authority to replace it. Why don't they teach us anything about the impossibility of economic calculation in the central planning? How easily can the authority of a teacher be replaced by the state authorities? And how can we keep the freedom when we spend the most important years of our lives in the jail?
Sorry for my horrible English; it is not so good in general and moreover I felt physically quite bad this time.

Presenting: Zdeňka Staňková and Urza (www.urza.cz) of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title: Prague Business Club: Who would build roads?
desc:
I was asked by entrepreneurs from the Prague Business Club to give a private lecture on transport infrastructure in the free market; I gladly accepted the offer and adapted the presentation to this target group, although the topic of course overlaps to a large extent (not completely) with the eleventh volume of the series Anarcho-capitalism from Polis.
If you are a skeptic and a practitioner of everyday reality, the lecture may be a little too optimistic and "visionary" for your taste; in that case, I recommend watching the lecture of the same name from the series Anarchocapitalism instead. Either way, the direction of the questions in the discussion is very different in both cases.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: The Fight for Democracy (Urza vs. Bob Kartous)
desc: Freedom of Learning hosted an unmoderated discussion between Bob Kartous and Urza on the topic of democracy in the education system in Paralelní Polis. We wish you a pleasant listening, although the debate was a bit heated in places and went into details.

title: A minor parallel
desc:
The state appears to be an indestructible entity that has been with us as far back as history, so that no reason can be seen why it should not endure forever; but a similar institution, of which one could assume exactly the same thing, was already there - and how do you think it turned out?

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Mises Academy 2017: Anarcho-Capitalism
desc:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is a record from the second of them - about anarcho-capitalism; the audience consisted of people interested in freedom and libertarianism, to which the lecture was tailored. A more detailed treatment of this topic aimed at a wider public can be found in the list of videos "Anarchocapitalism in Polis".

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Mises Academy 2017: Freedom to Learn
desc:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is the record of the first of these—of free education; the audience was overwhelmingly made up of libertarians who already know a lot about the given topic, to which the lecture was tailored. You can find a lecture on a similar topic aimed at a wider public in the video list "Anarchocapitalism in Polis" under the title "Anarchocapitalism, part seven: Education".

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: "LGBT Pride Week" Panel Discussion
desc:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on "LGBT Pride Week"; so it was originally called something else, but there were legal threats due to the trademark. Both proponents and opponents attended and there were many interesting views; you can find their montage in this video.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: About pedophilia and pedophiles
desc:
Although there are many statists in the LGBTQ community who try to push their agenda through state power, they are right about some things. We do not agree with violence through the state and restrictions on freedom of speech, because we are convinced that the right way is enlightenment.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: About science and evidence
desc:
During the lecture at the gymnasium in Holice, I mentioned that the theory of evolution is not proven; reactions were strong and often shocking.
In discussing this topic online and in person with a number of people, I realized that it would be a good idea to make a video explaining what scientific evidence actually means and the difference between it and a mere experiment that does not disprove a theory.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Engagement between heaven and earth
desc:
We've been on vacation, paragliding, engaged (in the air); we have an amazing life and we want to live it together. Even in this rather personal video you will find some anarcho-capitalist ideas, although this time they are exceptionally not the main topic.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Matěj Stropnický talks about weapons
desc:
After a long time, our MPs did something exceptionally, for which we even praised them; on the other hand, the chairman of the Greens, Matěj Stropnický, unsurprisingly sees it differently. And since he did not respond to the invitation to the discussion, we commented on his statement in the video.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: Lecture at the gymnasium in Holice
desc:
The students of the gymnasium in Holice invited me to the day of personalities to give them a lecture about anarcho-capitalism, freedom (and Freedom) of learning, education and the state; I gladly accepted and came, although the date conflicted with an invitation to the same event of another gymnasium.
Not only students and teachers arrived for the lecture, but to my surprise some parents too; in the end, an interesting debate was sparked, with the result of which I am certainly satisfied, but judge that for yourself.
Unfortunately, this is only an audio recording recorded on the phone, there is no picture, and the sound quality does not exactly allow for the most luxurious listening, for which I apologize; however, I find it listenable.
– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title: Panel Discussion "The Sharing Economy"
desc:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Sharing economy" - a phenomenon of today's time, an idol and a scarecrow. In-demand services that defeat established companies and scare the state with their success among users. 
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title: State versus innovation
desc:
Innovation can take place - and has for millennia - based on the voluntariness of resourceful and enterprising people; such a state is more than desirable and thanks to it our society continues to flourish. In addition, we unfortunately have an unrelenting, ravenous and expansive state that takes resources from the people against their will under the threat of using violence against them; even as a result of his interventions, various innovations arise, but at what cost?
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

title: Panel discussion "Anti-smoking law"
desc:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Anti-Smoking Law"; is the government supposed to "protect our health" or should no one be forced to conform the rules of their business to the orders of the powerful?
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Eleven: Who Would Build the Roads?
desc:
"If we had no state, who would build the roads?" So goes the most common question in libertarian jokes and one of the first reactions of statists to the mention of a stateless society; I am going to answer this very question at the lecture. And not only that! We will also talk about road traffic rules; would these differ from road to road if each road had its own private owner? After the lecture, as always, there will be a (perhaps heated) discussion; I look forward to hearing from you, especially if you disagree with me!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Ten: Public Space and Freedom of Speech
desc:
In the tenth lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism series, we will focus on public spaces and places "for all"; how could such spaces exist in a stateless society based on respect for property rights? Who would manage them, why and for what? Would all parks disappear in cities? Would we live in concrete jungles without a bit of greenery? In addition, we will talk about freedom of speech; how does it relate to the topic? We will show that very closely. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion; I hope you will oppose me!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Election of the (French) President
desc:

title: Anarcho-Capitalism Volume Nine: Weapons
desc:
The topic of the ninth lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be weapons and their regulation; we will talk about what the disarmament of society leads to and what is the main difference between a community of people with and without weapons. We will also look back in history and focus on a time and place when and where guns were virtually unregulated; what were the consequences? As always, the lecture will end with a discussion, in which you will be able to ask anything and, ideally, even oppose me.

title: Optimistic spring ride
desc:
Since we at FREEPORT CHANNEL usually rain fire and brimstone on the state, this time we decided to be positive, nice and share with you, dear viewers, a little happiness from a beautiful spring day; come for a ride with us xD

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Eight: Drugs
desc:
At the eighth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series, we will talk and discuss drugs; on the one hand, we will talk about the drugs themselves, but above all about the state's relationship to them and our freedom to deal with our own bodies as we see fit. We will also discuss the war on drugs that has been raging for decades; what did it actually cost us and what are its results? As usual, the lecture will be followed by a discussion, in which I will gladly try to answer all the questions you ask me.

title: LibertyCon 2017: State Education System
desc:
Presentation of Freedom to Learn at LibertyCon 2017.
The government is indoctrinating our kids with propaganda of statism and evil; the solution is the separation of state and education!

Presenting: Urza (www.urza.cz) and Zdeňka Staňková of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title: Anarcho-capitalism, part seven: Education
desc:
I consider this lecture to be the most important of the entire series on Anarcho-Capitalism; we will talk about the state education system as a powerful tool used to massively spread state propaganda. We will reveal the roots and effects of how current education works. Of course, there will also be an insight into how (and why) education could (and should) take place in a free market; and this time we will not only dwell on why it would not be such a horror as most people assume, but we will also look at the origin of those assumptions themselves. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion where I will answer all your questions and objections. Be sure to come this time!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title: Whitebeard votes but doesn't read
desc:
Member of Parliament Pavel Bělobárdek has publicly admitted that he does not read the laws he approves because we would like too much, after all, they are clouds of text.
We fear that the nature of the problem goes far beyond this case.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Six: Democracy
desc:
The topic of the sixth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle will be democracy, its harmfulness, but also a reflection on why it is so deified and, on the contrary, its criticism is considered something so inappropriate; we will also talk about why democracy quite naturally leads to socialism and how by supporting the irresponsible we create more irresponsible ones. As always, the lecture will be followed by my much-loved discussion; come and bring your friends who you think might be interested in this controversial topic.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Five: Culture
desc:
The topic of this lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism will be culture and art in the hands of the state and how they could function without it in the free market; although most people are convinced of the necessity of the state's role in this area, I believe that things are far from clear-cut. In addition to the creation of new art, we will also devote ourselves to the protection of already existing works of art and cultural monuments; can this also be provided on the market? As always, there will be an opportunity for discussion after the lecture.

desc:

Would maximum travel times for sparsely populated areas be guaranteed even in the free market? Shouldn't firefighters only rescue paying customers from burning houses and leave others to perish in the flames? As always, there will be an opportunity for discussion after the lecture.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Three: Money
desc:

We will also talk about how states are gradually devaluing this wonderful discovery through their interventions. You will be able to get an idea of fractional banking and find out why and how states cause cyclical economic crises through banks.

title: Anarcho-capitalism, part two: The state is a bad servant but a bad master
desc:
In the first lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, we talked about why the state is immoral. Come to the second lecture to hear why the state is even more inefficient. Anarcho-capitalism stands on two main pillars – natural law and the Austrian school of economics, the foundations of which will be presented at the lecture. But don't expect a dry talk about economics, we'll show everything with examples from the real world - for example, why does a top soccer player earn more than a firefighter who saves lives?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part One: The State Is Immoral
desc:
Come and listen to the introductory lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism! We talk about state funding and taxes; we will criticize the concept of taxes and their collection from the point of view of ethics. We will think through the consequences of what is behind every regulation and every law; how can their violent enforcement by the police be morally justified? And finally, we will say something about state propaganda and indoctrination; reasons why the state can basically do whatever it wants.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

title: Introduction
desc:
There are two of us. We love freedom. We love anarchy. We love capitalism. We love each other xD
We are talking about a free market stateless society; yes, we know how it looks, even we thought the idea was absurd at first...
However, try to give her a chance; you can always refuse it.
Motto: "Good people don't follow bad laws."
